title: The Health Centre
story: You and NOVA are volunteering at a school health centre when the doors lock for a fire check. NOVA is learning to answer students' questions about growing up. Its answers must be accurate before the doors open.
escaped: The doors open. NOVA now knows the glands and their hormones, uses data honestly and checks claims before answering questions about growing up.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's gland chart
locks.intro: NOVA has matched endocrine glands to the hormones they make. Tick the matches that are wrong.
locks.hint: Which gland is linked with diabetes when it doesn't make enough of its hormone?
locks.learn: Health answers built on mislabelled data could mislead people. That is why AI used for health must be trained on carefully checked information.

locks.title: Check NOVA's claim
locks.intro: A student asks NOVA how a baby's sex is decided. Is NOVA right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: The mother decides whether the baby will be a boy or a girl.
evidence: The baby's sex depends on whether the fertilised egg gets an X or a Y chromosome from the father's sperm.
Every unfertilised egg has an X chromosome.
Puberty usually begins between about 10 and 12 years of age.
locks.hint: Which parent's chromosome can be either X or Y?
locks.learn: An AI can repeat a wrong belief that many people hold. The textbook is clear: the mother is not responsible for the baby's sex. Checking against science stops AI spreading unfair ideas.

locks.title: Predict full height
locks.intro: The textbook gives the share of full adult height boys and girls usually reach at each age. NOVA wants to use it.
locks.question: A 12-year-old boy is 126 cm tall. What should NOVA tell him?
options: He'll probably reach about 150 cm (126 ÷ 84 × 100), but it's only an estimate: the table shows an average and people grow differently.
He will be exactly 150.0 cm tall.
He has stopped growing, so 126 cm.
Tables can't be used for anything.
locks.hint: He has reached 84% of his full height. And is everyone exactly average?
locks.learn: Predictions from averages are useful but never exact for one person. An honest AI gives the estimate and says how sure it can be, as the textbook does.

locks.title: Endocrine gland or not?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort body parts into endocrine glands (release hormones into the blood) and other organs. Choose its clues.
locks.hint: The voice box is in the neck, like the thyroid. The pancreas is in the abdomen, like the stomach.
locks.learn: Where an organ sits doesn't tell you what it does. NOVA needs the clue that defines an endocrine gland: releasing hormones into the blood.
